# WorkstationPaletteBridgeNL waits on a zero-width dock reveal, so three arms expire before the painted headers are ever consulted

## The Symptom

Three of `WorkstationPaletteBridgeNL`'s four arms fail on `dev`, each burning a full 60s on the same line of shared setup:

```
TimeoutError: page.waitForSelector: Timeout 60000ms exceeded.
  - waiting for locator('.neo-tab-header-button') to be visible
```

The fourth arm passes in 408ms — it is the pop-out one, which boots a different host.

## The Mechanism

Same defect class as `#18410`, one selector along.

`waitForSelector` resolves the **first** match in document order and, at its default `state: 'visible'`, waits for that element. Measured in the running app: the first `.neo-tab-header-toolbar` in document order is a **collapsed dock reveal** with `clientWidth: 0`, and its title carries `neo-tab-header-button` among its classes:

```
neo-dashboard-dock-reveal-title neo-tab-overflow-capped neo-tab-header-button neo-button no-text icon-left pressed
```

A zero-width element is never visible to Playwright, so the wait can only expire. The six real headers — carrying tab buttons 55px to 149px wide — are painted the whole time and are never consulted, because the query never reaches them.

The spec's own author had already met this hazard one line below and solved it there:

```js
// `attached`, not the default `visible`: the engine set is focus-gated, so `pin` and `maximize`
// rest at `visibility: hidden` with their geometry preserved.
await page.waitForSelector('.neo-toolbar-action', {state: 'attached', timeout: 60000})
```

The tab-header wait above it did not get the same treatment, and a reveal is a second way for a first match to be unpaintable.

## The Fix

Scope the readiness wait to a header that is not a reveal. `state: 'attached'` would also stop the timeout but weakens the signal — the intent is *"the app has painted a real tab header"*, which is worth keeping.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The three timing-out arms pass, and the pop-out arm still passes.
- [ ] The wait cannot resolve to a `.neo-dashboard-dock-reveal-header` descendant.
- [ ] The readiness signal stays visibility-based rather than degrading to `attached`.
- [ ] Total runtime drops from ~3.1m (three 60s expiries) to the sub-second range the passing arm already demonstrates.

## Out of Scope

- `WorkstationStarvedGeometryNL:64`, the sixth red, which has not been probed and is not claimed by this mechanism.
- The reveal's own markup. Carrying `neo-tab-header-button` on a reveal title is not obviously wrong; the specs that assume the class implies a paintable tab are.

## Related

- `#18410` — the same document-order substitution, one selector along, with the DOM census this ticket relies on.
